core_obligations: Reduce to types with no proper fibrations: from an analysis of p over A, the invariant F_ind(p) is bounded by the invariants of the first type in the analysis and of the generic fibres, so it suffices to treat the case where p has no proper fibrations (proof line 446).

Split by the dichotomy: by the cited classification result, such a p is interalgebraic over A either with finitely many independent realizations of a locally modular minimal type, or with a type internal to a non-locally-modular type (proof lines 446-450).
First case: both invariants equal 1 (proof line 451).

Second case: if the binding group relative to the constants is not generically 2-transitive then the fibre dimension is 1 and the non-minimality degree is bounded by it, so the two agree; otherwise, after reducing to an internal type, the binding group is definably isomorphic to an algebraic group action classified by Knop, and taking a Morley sequence on a line shows that both invariants equal 2 (proof lines 451-455).
proof_roadmap: Reduce along an analysis of the type to the fibration-free case (proof line 446).

Use the locally-modular/non-locally-modular dichotomy, and in the second case the generic transitivity of the binding group together with Knop's classification, to compute both invariants case by case (proof lines 446-455).
difficulty_reason: The proposition states that in the theory of differentially closed fields the non-minimality degree of a type agrees with its fibre dimension F_ind (statement lines 442-444). The proof first reduces to types without proper fibrations through the behaviour of F_ind along an analysis, then invokes the classification of such types into a locally modular case and a case internal to a non-locally-modular type (proof line 446-451). The step that carries the content is the second case: the proof has to move from generic 2-transitivity of the binding group to a definable isomorphism with a multiply transitive algebraic group action, where Knop's classification leaves only the affine and the projective actions, and then exhibit a Morley sequence on a line to obtain the value 2 for both invariants (proof lines 451-455). The first case is immediate, and the reduction is a citation plus one estimate. H2.
